title: The Garden of the Glass Steppe Revisited
premise: Ivo Zhou keeps accounts for the Ledger Guild, whose clerks trade in impossible commodities—bottled grief, borrowed luck, the last words of the drowned. When a dying courier leaves them a map of Vessany, a country erased from every atlas twenty years ago, Ivo realizes the guild's founding ledgers were stolen from Vessany's silent god, and that the god's silence is the long winter itself. Pursued by guild enforcers and haunted by the memories the map unseals, Ivo gathers a found family of debtors and deserters to reach the one door back into Vessany before winter seals it forever. At the threshold, Ivo must choose: restore the god and the country at the cost of their own remembered life, or burn the ledgers and let justice be done by people instead of powers. They burn them—and walk out of the snow carrying a new ledger with only their found family's names in it.
about_author: Ines Villalobos is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the property records of towns that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about paperwork, grief, and the stubborn arithmetic of belonging, and live somewhere with very short winters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Unpaid Things
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. In the Ledger Guild's counting house, Ivo audits a shipment of bottled grief and quietly falsifies an entry to save a debtor from indenture. The chapter establishes the guild's cold economy and Ivo's small, illegal mercies. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: A Courier Dies Owed
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A frostbitten stranger collapses in the guild's doorway, presses a wax-sealed map into Ivo's hands, and dies whispering the name of a country Ivo has never heard of: Vessany. The map burns cold to the touch. Emotional beat: dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Remember
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cross-checking the map against the guild's founding ledgers, Ivo discovers pages torn out and a god's name scraped away. The senior clerk, Maren, catches them and warns them to forget it—too late, since Ivo's own memories have begun returning unbidden. Emotional beat: the vertigo of recovered memory.

chapters.title: The Debtor's Daughter
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV, a smuggler indentured to the guild. Ivo offers to erase her family's debt if she'll guide them toward the door out of the country. She agrees for her own reasons. Emotional beat: wary first trust, the first stone of the found family.

chapters.title: Enforcers at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Alternating Ivo and Sefa. Guild enforcers raid the counting house; Ivo flees with the founding ledger's stolen spine, and the group gains a third member—Brother Anselm, a defrocked priest who once served Vessany's silent god. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Country That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. On the road north, Anselm explains the erasure: Vessany's god was silenced by a bargain its own clergy made, and the guild's ledgers hold the terms. Ivo's memories sharpen—they were born there. Emotional beat: grief for a homeland that officially never existed.

chapters.title: Winter's Long Falling
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The party shelters with a village of Vessany exiles who trade memories like currency. Maren arrives, not as hunter but as penitent, revealing she tore the pages to hide her own part in the silencing. Emotional beat: forgiveness extended and not yet accepted.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Nowhere
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Guided by the map and the exiles' pooled memories, the party finds the threshold—a door standing free in a snowfield, opening onto Vessany's unfallen summer. Enforcers close in behind. Emotional beat: terror and wonder braided together at the threshold.

chapters.title: The Silent God Speaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Inside, the god is not dead but waiting, and it offers restoration at a price: the ledgers' terms must be paid in a life's worth of memory. Ivo realizes the guild's whole trade was this god, harvested. Emotional beat: the climax's terrible clarity—justice cannot be outsourced.

chapters.title: A New Ledger, Few Names
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing. Ivo burns the founding ledgers, breaking the bargain and letting Vessany's people—not its god—decide their own return. The winter stops falling. Ivo, lighter and half-emptied, walks back through the door to the family that stayed. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; memory as a thing given, not kept.
